judgments.catchwords: Administrative Law – Judicial review – Duty of candour – Public authority – Duty to make full and fair disclosure of all material facts – Failure to disclose that Valuation List being amended had expired – Breach of duty of candour – Consequences. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Statutory lifespan – Section 137 Local Government Act 1976 – New Valuation List must be prepared once every five years – Valuation List expires after five years – No local authority may use Valuation List for indeterminable period. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Amendment – Section 144 Local Government Act 1976 – Amendment can only be made to current Valuation List – Not to expired or outdated Valuation List – Amendment to expired list is ultra vires and void. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Section 137(2) – Saving provision – Valuation List remains in force until superseded by new list – Not a power to extend lifespan of existing list – Only temporary measure while new list being prepared– Extension of time – Section 137(3) – State Authority may extend period for preparation of new Valuation List – Not power to extend validity of existing Valuation List – No extension granted in present case. Local Government Law – Retrospective rates – Amendment to current Valuation List may have retrospective effect – But no retrospective effect where Valuation List itself has expired – Question of retrospectivity becomes academic.

judgments.catchwords: CRIMINAL LAW: Dangerous Drugs – Trafficking – Possession – Knowledge – Charge under s. 39B(1)(a) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 – Statutory presumption of trafficking under s. 37(da) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 – Statutory presumption of possession under s. 37(d) Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 – Whether possession established by direct evidence obviates reliance on statutory presumption of possession – Whether cumulative invocation of presumptions of possession and trafficking amounts to impermissible double presumption – Whether concealment of drugs within vehicle falls within definition of "keeping", "concealing" or "storing" so as to constitute trafficking – Whether exclusive and continuous custody and control of vehicle over extended period supports inference of knowledge – Whether sole possession of key affording exclusive means of access to place of concealment establishes exclusivity of possession notwithstanding public accessibility of parking area – Whether elaborate manner of concealment is exculpatory or inculpatory of accused's knowledge – Whether accused's use of a different class of drug negates knowledge of trafficked drug – Whether accused's own recent use of vehicle and physical contact with altered seat renders denial of knowledge implausible – Whether bare denial of knowledge, unsupported by positive evidence, sufficient to rebut presumption of trafficking on balance of probabilities CRIMINAL PROCEDURE: Criminal Trial – Continuation of Part-Heard Trial – Duty of Court – Whether successor judge, upon retirement of change in presiding judge – Duty of court at close of prosecution's case under s. 180(1) Criminal Procedure Code – Requirement of maximum evaluation of credibility and reliability of prosecution evidence – Whether inference favourable to accused ought to be preferred where evidence admits of more than one inference – Duty of court at conclusion of trial under s. 182A(1) Criminal Procedure Code – Whether defence evidence, taken with whole of evidence, displaces prima facie finding – Whether accused's explanation, if believed or raising reasonable doubt, entitles accused to acquittal – Standard and definition of reasonable doubt EVIDENCE: Admissibility – Adverse Inference – Identity of Exhibits – Information leading to discovery under s. 27 Evidence Act 1950 – Requirement that exact words used by accused be proved – Requirement of caution prior to admission of confession – Conduct of accused admissible under s. 8 Evidence Act 1950 – Whether conduct must bear direct and immediate relationship to fact in issue and not be conduct brought about by another agency – Whether intoxication negates voluntariness of accused's conduct – Whether discrepancy or absence of accessory parts of locus exhibit affects identity of drug exhibit – Whether defect in completeness of physical exhibit distinguishable from defect in chain of custody connecting drugs seized to drugs analysed – Effect of unchallenged expert/chemist evidence – Whether failure to cross-examine on crucial issue amounts to acceptance of testimony – Whether adverse inference under s. 114(g) Evidence Act 1950 may be drawn against prosecution for non-production of fingerprint or CCTV evidence or non-calling of registered owner as witness – Conditions for drawing adverse inference against prosecution – Whether prosecution obliged to call every possible witness – Whether exculpatory account raised for the first time at trial amounts to recent fabrication properly weighed against credibility of defence – Whether such treatment infringes accused's right to silence CRIMINAL PROCEDURE: Sentencing – Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 (Act 846)
